title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation ratio for metric TSP
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: Determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{TSP}}\), the infimum of achievable expected polynomial-time approximation ratios for the symmetric metric traveling salesman problem.
definitions: An instance is an integer \(n\ge3\) and an explicitly listed symmetric rational distance matrix \(d\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}^{n\times n}\), with \(d(i,i)=0\), \(d(i,j)>0\) for i unequal to j, and \(d(i,k)\le d(i,j)+d(j,k)\) for all triples. A feasible tour is a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), of cost \(\sum_{i=1}^{n}d(\pi(i),\pi(i+1))\), where \(\pi(n+1)=\pi(1)\). OPT is the minimum over these tours. The metric is arbitrary, without Euclidean or graph-family restrictions. An algorithm is a uniform randomized Turing machine with independent fair random bits. Its worst-case running time, over all random tapes, is polynomial in the binary input length. It always returns a feasible solution, and its expected cost is measured over its coins. A real number \(r\ge1\) is achievable if one such algorithm satisfies \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{cost}(A(I))]\le r\operatorname{OPT}(I)\) for every valid instance I. The target is the infimum of achievable r; the polynomial and algorithm may depend on r. An infimum need not be attained. All integers and rational input data use explicit binary encodings, with numerator and positive denominator for each rational; their full lengths count toward the input size. No complexity assumption is built into the definition.

context_blocks.text: The scientific target is the best approximation achievable by any efficient algorithm. The subtour-LP gap is a different quantity: it compares the optimum tour with the value of one particular fractional relaxation.
The 2021 breakthrough produces expected approximation strictly below 3/2. Its theorem measures against the optimum integral tour, which matches this card’s definition.

why: Determine the fundamental efficient-approximation limit of the canonical routing problem, beyond the guarantees of any one linear relaxation or rounding algorithm.

answer_criterion: Supply a real number a and a complete Lean-checked proof that its absolute difference from the defined constant is at most \(1/100\). A proved containing interval of width at most \(1/50\) qualifies through its midpoint. The constant is unconditional: a lower bound relying on an unproved complexity assumption settles only the corresponding conditional statement. Merely restating the defining infimum is not a determination.

sentences: Metric TSP asks for a shortest tour through every point of an arbitrary finite metric.
This card asks for the best expected ratio achievable by any uniform randomized polynomial-time algorithm.
The ratio compares a returned tour with the optimal tour, not with an LP solution.
The breakthrough below 3/2 leaves the ultimate approximation threshold undetermined.
A Lean-certified estimate within absolute error 0.01 must bound the algorithmic infimum on both sides.
